title: Candidiasis (vulvo-vaginal infection)
summary: See NICE CKS and BASHH national guideline for the management of vulvovaginal candidiasis. Advise patient to consider self-referral to the community pharmacy Pharmacy First Service should they experience this condition in the future (see BSO website). For severe or recurrent infection refer to NICE CKS or BASHH.
changeSummary: Initial transcription from Eolas Medical, Northern Ireland Primary Care Antimicrobial Guidelines (v5.119.0).
clinicalNotes: Fluconazole capsules should not be used in pregnancy or risk of pregnancy.
Clotrimazole damages latex condoms and diaphragms – counselling required.
For other alternative treatment regimens refer to NICE CKS.

regimens.label: Adult acute infection – oral fluconazole
restrictions: Not to be used in pregnancy or risk of pregnancy.
notes: If there are signs of severe infection repeat after 72 hours, i.e. fluconazole 150 mg oral capsule on day 1 and day 4.
If there are vulval symptoms consider clotrimazole 1% or 2% cream applied 2–3 times a day for up to 14 days.

regimens.label: Adult acute infection – if oral therapy is contraindicated (intravaginal pessary)

components.dose: 500 mg as a single dose at night

notes: If there are signs of severe infection repeat after 72 hours, i.e. clotrimazole 500 mg pessary (2 pessaries) – insert 1 pessary intravaginally on day 1 and day 4.
If there are vulval symptoms consider clotrimazole 1% or 2% cream applied 2–3 times a day for up to 14 days.

regimens.label: Adult – alternative if oral fluconazole or clotrimazole 500 mg pessary contraindicated or not tolerated

components.dose: 5 g intravaginally as a single dose at night

clinicalValidation.reviewNotes: Transcribed from Eolas Medical; not yet clinically validated.
